response: Yes, peritoneal dialysis can affect halitosis in patients with end-stage renal disease. Studies have shown that patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis may experience a reduction in halitosis, also known as bad breath, due to the removal of uremic toxins from the body. Uremic toxins, which can contribute to halitosis, are waste products that build up in the blood when the kidneys are not functioning properly. By removing these toxins, peritoneal dialysis can help alleviate halitosis and improve oral health in patients with end-stage renal disease.
